audit.whatIsWrong: Vex's ultimate is called 'Doombringer' in eight separate places and described as an execute.
audit.why: Her R is Shadow Surge (140/120/100s, 2000/2500/3000 range): it fires a missile that MARKS a champion and recasts into a dash. Riot's text describes no execute threshold. The name is fabricated and the mechanic is misdescribed — a reader waits for a health threshold that does not exist instead of watching for the mark.
audit.corrected: Shadow Surge named throughout and described as mark-then-dash, with its 140s rank-1 cooldown and 2000 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The shield is repeatedly credited to her passive ('passive shield from CC procs', 'passive shield uptime', 'passive shield stacks').
audit.why: The shield is Personal Space (W, 16/15/14/13/12s, 475 range) — a short-range shield plus nearby damage. The passive, Doom 'n Gloom, empowers her next basic ability to fear and interrupt dashes, and recharges faster when nearby enemies dash. Anivia never dashes, so that discount never applies to her: the fear comes back on its base timer.
audit.corrected: Shield attributed to Personal Space with its cooldown and 475 range; fear attributed to Doom 'n Gloom with the glow as the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..4].side read 'Skill' against win[0..4] 'Vex', and the packet flags the chart as contradicting the data (Vex 5/7 stages while Anivia wins 53.29%).
audit.why: Levels 1-4 genuinely belong to Vex on range and shield uptime, so those rows align to Vex. Level 6, however, was given to Vex solely on the fabricated 'Doombringer execute' — with that gone, Glacial Storm's zone plus Rebirth is the real level-6 story, and the 53.29% win rate supports the flip.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-4 to Vex on the full layer; Level 6 flipped to Anivia on BOTH layers as a matched pair, leaving Vex 4 / Anivia 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carried a cooldown; the packet counts a single sequencing cue for the whole matchup.
audit.why: Personal Space (16s at rank 1) and Shadow Surge (140s at rank 1) are the two clocks that decide when you may step forward.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into the cooldown, do's and don'ts lines.

edits.after: - Personal Space is her shield: 16s at rank 1 and only 475 range, so poke from 1075 and it shields nothing. - Doom 'n Gloom recharges faster off nearby dashes and you never dash, so her fear returns on its slow base timer. - Shadow Surge is 140s.

edits.before: Anivia is fully outclassed level 1-2 — Vex's Q spam and passive shield off CC punish any trade attempt, and your kit has nothing to answer with yet. This stays rough through levels 3-5 since her mobility (however clunky) and burst threaten you every time you go for a Q-W setup, and a landed fear only makes it worse. From level 6 her Doombringer execute is the peak danger point, so play maximally passive and farm safely under tower rather than contest CS in poke range.
edits.after: Anivia is fully outclassed level 1-2 — Mistral Bolt reaches 1200 and Personal Space shields whatever you poke back, so trades only go one way. This stays rough through levels 3-5 since Looming Darkness slows you into her follow-up every time you set up a Q-W, and a landed Doom 'n Gloom fear only makes it worse. From level 6 Shadow Surge marks you from 2000 units and dashes in, so farm safely under tower rather than contest CS in her poke range.

edits.before: Once your Rylai's comes online, the tide starts to turn — you finally land Q reliably enough to threaten a wall-trap, closing the gap that Vex enjoyed for the whole early game. Keep farming safely and avoid all-in windows until you have that first completed item; trying to out-poke her before then is a losing fight. Ping her Doombringer cooldown to your team since it remains her single biggest kill threat on you specifically.
edits.after: Once your Rylai's comes online, the tide starts to turn — you finally land Q reliably enough to threaten a wall-trap, closing the gap that Vex enjoyed for the whole early game. Keep farming safely and avoid all-in windows until you have that first completed item; trying to out-poke her before then is a losing fight. Ping Shadow Surge, 140 seconds at rank 1, since that mark is her single biggest kill threat on you.

edits.before: With a full combo and Rylai's active slow, wall-stunning Vex into Glacial Storm deletes her squishy HP pool before she can reposition for a safe Doombringer angle. Rebirth is a genuine advantage here — it buys the extra half-second that turns her execute attempt into your winning trade instead. Group around your wall in teamfights and force her to commit first; that's where Anivia finally wins the exchange.

notes: 'Doombringer' is not a Vex ability — her R is Shadow Surge, and it marks and dashes rather than executing. The fabricated name appeared in eight places and the fabricated execute mechanic drove the level-6 chart row, which is why that row is flipped. The chart flip on Level 6 is proposed as a matched pair (phases[4].side + win[4]) and is Medium confidence: it follows the packet's own defect note that the chart contradicts a 53.29% Anivia win rate, and removing the invented execute leaves no reason to give Vex the row against Glacial Storm plus Rebirth. Rows 1-4 aligned to Vex to match win[0..3] and the packet. Vex's Doom 'n Gloom anti-dash mark never applies to Anivia, so it is written only as the reason her fear recharges slowly here, never as a negative. | COHERENCE: 4 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
